newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas board split on Generale deal - papers.
newsitem.headline: Havas board split on Generale deal - papers.

text.p: The supervisory board of media group Havas was not unanimous in accepting a deal with Generale des Eaux about the transfer of a stake of Canal Plus, the Les Echos and Financial Times newspapers said.
The papers said that France Telecom and Lyonnaise des Eaux expressed reluctance over the deal.

Pierre Dauzier, chairman of Havas, told Les Echos in an interview that "the majority of the shareholders concerned are satisfied," and he said it was possible that Paribas and Caisse des Depots et des Consignations could sell their small stakes.

The deal under which Generale des Eaux takes a 30 percent stake in Havas and transfers its Canal Plus stake and its fully-owned Generale d'Images unit to Havas in a deal worth some six billion francs, will strengthen the position of Generale's telecommunications unit Cegetel in multimedia.
It will also make Havas and Canal Plus stronger companies with a solid capital structure.
Cegetel rivals France Telecom while Lyonnaise des Eaux is a big cable television operator.
